nodes.norm_label: partial companion failure without conductor rollback
nodes.rationale: Each tool has an independent outcome. FAILED yields partial code 3 while preserving already verified Conductor; the shell wrapper and global lifecycle coordinator use the same contract.

nodes.label: PATH priority and actual command readiness
nodes.norm_label: path priority and actual command readiness
nodes.rationale: An exact new binary passing --version is insufficient if normal PATH resolution still selects the old tool. Readiness also requires effective command resolution and installed wiring.

nodes.label: Provider identity and ownership boundary
nodes.rationale: Managed receipts and verified uv/Cargo metadata distinguish recognized tools from unknown programs. crates.io rtk is a different project; unknown tools remain unchanged with a failure/skip explanation.

nodes.label: Per-tool status records
nodes.rationale: Records expose tool/status/before/after/latest/detail and CURRENT, UPDATED, INSTALLED, AVAILABLE, ABSENT, SKIPPED or FAILED. Offline discovery and shadowed commands must not be reported CURRENT/UPDATED.

nodes.label: Companion review focus
nodes.rationale: Prioritize PATH shadowing, pinned uv upgrades, replacing the active Graphify interpreter, unusable latest releases and personally edited skills; each needs a negative test.

nodes.label: Graphify skill ownership and preservation
nodes.rationale: Package/original registered content can be refreshed; personally edited skill files are preserved with a conflict and FAILED readiness. MCP/project hooks remain out of scope.

nodes.label: Official stable release selection
nodes.rationale: Query official RTK release assets/checksums and non-yanked stable PyPI graphifyy metadata. Do not inherit a third-party package index or silently downgrade to an older release when latest is unsupported.

nodes.label: Superpowers installation-only compatibility
nodes.rationale: Existing Superpowers installation/enabling behavior stays in the shell entry point; this plan does not add automatic Superpowers upgrades and preserves --skip-companions.

nodes.label: sync(paths, mode, skip) coordination contract
nodes.rationale: Install/update/check share a coordinator returning per-tool records in rtk, graphify order. It uses the caller's common lock rather than re-entering it, and CONDUCTOR_COMPANION_HOME must be absolute and canonical.

nodes.label: upgrade and probe contracts
nodes.rationale: upgrade(found, name, version, root, profile) returns a verified executable; probe checks actual launch and exact expected version. An error restores only verified own changes and then raises.

nodes.label: Pinned uv upgrade false-success trap
nodes.rationale: A manager exit code 0 with the old pinned version is not latest-version success. Tests must verify executable version and manager metadata rather than receipt existence.

nodes.label: Final-path versioned Graphify environment
nodes.rationale: Create the virtual environment directly at its final versioned path because moving a venv breaks embedded paths. Receipts and backups live outside the removable Conductor runtime.

nodes.label: wire executable and owned configuration
nodes.rationale: Wire only a verified executable using isolated HOME/USERPROFILE/config during checks, compare owned records and preserve foreign hooks/settings. Existing Graphify skill content is checked, not merely its presence.

nodes.label: Windows/Linux lifecycle acceptance
nodes.rationale: Exercise installed launchers and no-clone install/update/uninstall in isolated profiles, preserve private data and literal special-character paths, cover fault points and platform skips, and separate fake transport from real network checks.

nodes.label: Bootstrap revision inside the shared operation
nodes.norm_label: bootstrap revision inside the shared operation
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap supplies its verified source SHA to the common operation, not a receipt written outside the lock. Dirty local source has no claimed clean revision.

nodes.label: Common pending journal and recovery
nodes.rationale: Before writes, create the snapshot then an atomic pending record in private state; verify payload, write state last and clear pending only after confirmation. Existing schema-1 snapshots remain valid for rollback.

nodes.label: Lifecycle companion synchronization
nodes.rationale: Use companions.sync for install/update/check even when Conductor SHA is current; a companion failure preserves verified Conductor. One caller-held lock spans both phases without nested acquisition, and status/check only report pending.

nodes.label: Compatible shell and helper entry points
nodes.norm_label: compatible shell and helper entry points
nodes.rationale: install.sh, install-global.sh, uninstall.sh and install preflight/receipt/CLI helpers delegate to the same mechanism rather than maintaining a second write algorithm.

nodes.label: Conditional byte and mode recovery
nodes.rationale: Recovery checks bytes and POSIX modes including readback. Mode-only edits after interruption are conflicts; both available states are preserved rather than overwritten.

nodes.label: Coherent delivery, documentation and graph freshness
nodes.norm_label: coherent delivery, documentation and graph freshness
nodes.rationale: Update RU/EN/AZ README, HANDOFF and CHANGELOG before one final Graphify update. Match staged changes to proof; publishing and GitHub CI have distinct status, and successful extraction alone is not published-graph verification.

nodes.label: Global lifecycle exit-code contract
nodes.rationale: 0 confirms the entire requested flow, 1 means Conductor error, 2 invalid arguments, 3 verified Conductor but incomplete companions, and 130 interruption. Explicit skip or absent tools during update are not failures.

nodes.label: One profile-wide lifecycle
nodes.rationale: One profile installation serves every project on Windows/Git Bash and Linux. Personal lessons, evidence, model settings, working Git, project rules and independent tools are not replacement payload. No GUI, service, database or Python-crash investigation is added.

nodes.label: Lifecycle implementation and evidence status
nodes.rationale: Opening status records tasks 1-4 implemented, commit 3ce180a, checked live Russian install and local Windows/Linux results. The historical closing checklist still says the live install had not changed; this stale statement must not silently override current status.

nodes.label: prepare_install, verify and apply_install contracts
nodes.rationale: prepare_install accepts source, scopes, reply, skip_values and revision and returns UpdatePlan; verify uses the supplied new scopes, while the existing prepare update contract remains.

nodes.label: Full-content legacy cleanup and exact Git origin
nodes.norm_label: full-content legacy cleanup and exact git origin
nodes.rationale: Retired files may be removed only by complete known content after snapshot. Git config changes require the actual global origin within the profile and exact old Conductor value; unknown origins or mixed templates are retained with a warning.

nodes.label: Paths, UpdatePlan and Transaction architecture
nodes.rationale: Reuse the existing path targets, prepared change plan and transaction snapshot format. installation/removal prepare operations, cli coordinates them, recovery handles pending work and payload remains the single renderer.

nodes.label: Source-based restoration after uninstall
nodes.rationale: Print the concrete Python cli.py --config --profile rollback --backup command with real paths. Do not promise that the now-removed conductor command can restore itself.

nodes.label: Opt-in project sweep outside global transaction
nodes.norm_label: opt-in project sweep outside global transaction
nodes.rationale: Standalone --sweep-roots remains explicit and uses checked project-artifacts ownership. It is not one atomic transaction spanning all projects and the global installation.

nodes.label: pending and recover contracts
nodes.rationale: pending validates and reports without writes; recover is invoked only inside exclusive(paths), uses a verified own-installation snapshot and accepts only recorded before/after states.

nodes.label: prepare_removal and apply_removal contracts
nodes.rationale: CLI and standalone removal share the plan and apply contract. Lessons are kept by default; explicit --remove-lessons requests their removal and --keep-lessons remains compatible.

nodes.label: Conservative removal ownership
nodes.rationale: Only positively identified owned files are removed under the same snapshot/lock. Unknown leftovers and ambiguous manifestless state cause preservation/refusal; personal global CLAUDE.md is never removed.

nodes.label: Lifecycle review focus
nodes.rationale: Review interruption after file verification, mode-only late edits, global targets without checkout, Windows self-removal exit status and conservative behavior for missing state or mixed directories.

nodes.label: Preserved scopes and single language choice
nodes.norm_label: preserved scopes and single language choice
nodes.rationale: Render all files before writing; choose language once, merge selected scopes with registered components and keep --skip-global-md. First personal-rule overwrite warns and snapshots; subsequent manual edits cause refusal.

nodes.label: Owned JSON hook leaves
nodes.rationale: Reuse settings-json install/strip ownership parsing. Malformed or duplicate-key JSON is rejected and foreign hooks/settings remain intact; Cursor and Antigravity changes are explicit transaction targets.

nodes.label: Installer recovery without partial runtime imports
nodes.norm_label: installer recovery without partial runtime imports
nodes.rationale: A killed child and a fresh complete-source installer prove recovery does not import a half-removed runtime. Fault injection is test-only, not a production bypass.

nodes.label: Windows conductor.cmd self-removal and exit status
nodes.norm_label: windows conductor.cmd self-removal and exit status
nodes.rationale: Test the installed .cmd, not just cli.py. Deleting a batch file must not cause its continuation or lose the actual exit code; restoration uses a complete source copy after the CLI is removed.

nodes.label: Fault, ownership and platform acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance covers scopes/languages, special-character literal paths, no-clone and checkout-free launchers, global/standalone equivalence, memory preservation, version-service failures, write/verify/crash fault injection, concurrent operations, POSIX modes and hostile paths/state. New guards must fail when disarmed.

nodes.label: Separate companion phase after Conductor
nodes.rationale: Start companions only after the successful Conductor transaction and report outcomes independently. A failed tool neither reverses Conductor nor becomes green readiness. No Superpowers auto-update or project Graphify rebuild is requested.

nodes.label: Completion and graph-source freshness boundary
nodes.rationale: Completion concerns the existing CLI risks and automatic RTK/Graphify flows, not new GUI or mandatory agent rules. Refresh Graphify once after a coherent change set; while code changes, files remain source truth.

nodes.label: Compare-before-write and conditional recovery
nodes.rationale: Compare the earlier observation before each write and read back bytes/modes after it. Restore only own changes; later foreign changes preserve both available states and yield a backup-path error.

nodes.label: Next-command interrupted-operation recovery
nodes.rationale: The next mutating command under the same lock restores a verified pending snapshot or refuses on conflict. rollback supports both install and update snapshots; status reports incompleteness rather than claiming health.

nodes.label: One global installation per user profile
nodes.norm_label: one global installation per user profile
nodes.rationale: All projects share one profile installation; project configuration stays separate. Preserve language, memory and personal rules with verifiable recovery. Windows/Git Bash and Linux plus RU/EN/AZ documentation are in scope, not GUI/services/accounts or Python-crash diagnosis.

nodes.label: Global install and reinstall flow
nodes.rationale: Keep no-clone terminal installation; installed conductor install uses the same global mechanism. Install missing RTK/Graphify and update existing copies unless explicitly skipped.

nodes.label: Single persisted language decision
nodes.rationale: Use explicit language, otherwise a dialog with stored choice, saved choice for noninteractive execution, then Russian default. Invalid parameters must not mutate installation.

nodes.label: Owned hook parsing and legacy cleanup
nodes.norm_label: owned hook parsing and legacy cleanup
nodes.rationale: Reuse the existing JSON hook-ownership parser, preserve foreign commands/keys, and list Cursor, Antigravity and Git edits explicitly in the plan. Known retired files require bounded ownership and snapshots; unknown or mixed directories are never wholesale-deleted.

nodes.label: Managed-copy migration of recognized uv/Cargo tools
nodes.norm_label: managed-copy migration of recognized uv/cargo tools
nodes.rationale: The user-approved clarification creates separate managed copies with verified PATH priority while preserving original programs and manager data. Instructions update only if equal to original or registered content; unknown programs and personal edits remain unclaimed.

nodes.label: First-install and reinstall ownership rules
nodes.rationale: Repeat install refuses changed managed files. First explicit overwrite of personal rules requires a visible warning and verified recoverable snapshot; --skip-global-md preserves CLAUDE.md and a foreign conductor command is never overwritten.

nodes.label: Private pending journal and lock lifetime
nodes.norm_label: private pending journal and lock lifetime
nodes.rationale: Store the snapshot and pending journal outside runtime before the first write, holding the common lock through verification and journal close. Atomicity is per file, not the whole tree.

nodes.label: Validated preparation and payload rendering
nodes.rationale: Validate arguments, dependencies, readable source and link-free paths, then lock. A prepared list records prior/expected bytes and modes, components, provenance and checks; payload.py remains the sole renderer.

nodes.label: Prepared change set and shared transaction
nodes.norm_label: prepared change set and shared transaction
nodes.rationale: Selected approach computes exact new files and permitted settings edits before snapshot and verification. Reusing the existing Python mechanism gives unified ownership/recovery while shell commands remain compatible.

nodes.label: Private data and component preservation
nodes.rationale: Lessons, verification results, model settings, keys and targets outside the allowlist are not replacement payload. Selecting a scope does not implicitly remove other registered components.

nodes.label: Wrapper-around-existing-scripts alternative
nodes.rationale: Rejected as the main design because unknown script side effects make partial writes indistinguishable from later personal edits without precomputed expected content.

nodes.label: Lifecycle design selection criteria
nodes.rationale: Prioritize no unexplained overwrite, backup before first mutation, one shared lock, ordinary-error and process-crash recovery, consistent CLI/script behavior and command/language/memory compatibility.

nodes.label: Latest stable RTK/Graphify synchronization
nodes.rationale: Every normal install/reinstall/update checks stable releases for existing RTK/Graphify copies; install adds missing tools and update does not. Working is not necessarily current; explicit skip/read-only check are exceptions and prereleases are excluded.

nodes.label: Global CLI and standalone uninstall equivalence
nodes.norm_label: global cli and standalone uninstall equivalence
nodes.rationale: Conductor uninstall and uninstall.sh share behavior. Independent RTK, Graphify, Superpowers and project rules remain; lesson preservation/removal is explicit. status and rollback are retained.

nodes.label: Global update and read-only check
nodes.rationale: Update Conductor and installed RTK/Graphify even when Conductor is current; do not introduce absent tools. update --check performs no installation or other mutations.

nodes.label: Version stamp after executable verification
nodes.rationale: Stamp the new version only after checking new installed entry points and exact hook registrations, independently of any old revision marker. Failed verification cannot claim the new version installed.

nodes.label: bootstrap.sh (reference in HANDOFF.md)
nodes.rationale: Downloads tools/bootstrap.py to obtain the official commit archive without cloning; needs Python 3.10+, Git and Bash.

nodes.label: install.ps1 (reference in HANDOFF.md)
nodes.rationale: Windows bootstrap uses Git Bash rather than WSL and delegates archive download through tools/bootstrap.py.

nodes.label: tools/bootstrap.py (reference in HANDOFF.md)
nodes.rationale: Fetches an archive for a concrete official GitHub commit into a temporary folder.

nodes.label: Unified install and GitHub bootstrap tests
nodes.norm_label: unified install and github bootstrap tests
nodes.rationale: Uses python -B unittest discovery in qa/bootstrap with verbose output.

nodes.label: docs/superpowers/specs/
nodes.rationale: Спецификация заморожена и не обновляется, чтобы HANDOFF.md и CHANGELOG.md оставались единственным источником истины о текущем состоянии правил, а не дублировали и не расходились с устаревшим документом.

nodes.label: qa/reports/
nodes.rationale: Никогда не попадает в runtime-дерево, чтобы измерения контрольной группы не смешивались с исполняемой сборкой.

nodes.label: docs/memory-recovery.md (восстановление приватного репозитория и расписания)
nodes.rationale: Guide for restoring the complete private repository and Windows schedule, beyond ordinary lesson maintenance.

nodes.label: ~/.claude/conductor/lessons.md (входящее хранилище уроков)
nodes.rationale: Shared one-line capture inbox lives beside curated lessons and their index.

nodes.label: lessons/ + INDEX.md (разобранная память с индексом)
nodes.rationale: Separate indexed lesson files replace the old ten-line injection that left 142 lessons invisible; indexed reading scales without discarding stored knowledge.

nodes.label: qa/reports/lesson-recall-2026-09-26.log
nodes.rationale: Records 16 search checks, 10 delivery/maintenance checks, RU/EN/AZ installation and disabled-guard control; Windows skipped two privileged-link checks.

nodes.label: runtime/memory/recall.md (описание подбора уроков)
nodes.rationale: Guide explains task-based lesson retrieval and leaves maintenance/distillation policy unchanged.

nodes.label: runtime/memory/recall.py (подбор уроков по задаче)
nodes.rationale: Task terms retrieve candidates from inbox and curated full text; the agent judges context, recency only breaks ties and absence is not filled with unrelated lessons.

nodes.label: tools/migrate-lessons.sh (разбор уроков по файлам)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the lesson index from the store, installs into memory/ for checkout-free maintenance, places incomplete dates last and avoids same-second archive overwrites.

nodes.label: tools/schedule-memory-backup.ps1 (расписание бэкапа памяти на Windows)
nodes.rationale: The separate PowerShell script restores Windows scheduling only on explicit execution.

nodes.label: Плейсхолдер __CONDUCTOR_DIR__
nodes.rationale: __CONDUCTOR_DIR__ replaces an author-machine hardcoded path so other machines can load playbooks; installation renders it and lint/doctor guard it.

nodes.label: tools/doctor.sh (reference in CHANGELOG.md)
nodes.rationale: Doctor fails on an unrendered module base; release entries also add help flags and full-runtime checks.

nodes.label: qa/bench — A/B runner
nodes.rationale: Both arms exclude live user settings, each invocation has a separate workspace/evidence namespace, and an atomic manifest records commit, runtime digest and artifact identity.

nodes.label: qa/reports/ab-report-v2.md
nodes.rationale: The dated v2.1.1 entry reports 27/27 traps at n=5 in both arms and reproduce-first in 12/12 debug reruns, with two extra median turns.

nodes.label: core.md
nodes.rationale: The August entry defers redundant core edits for lack of space; a later historical entry explains fixing its hardcoded module base.

nodes.label: settings-json.py leaf ownership
nodes.rationale: Only owned hook-command leaves are removed while foreign neighbors in the same entry survive.

nodes.label: audit-hooks (read-only проверка хуков)
nodes.rationale: Read-only structural audit checks exact events, matchers, commands and timeouts instead of relying on textual grep.

nodes.label: install-companions.sh (reference in README.en.md)
nodes.rationale: After Conductor verification, Superpowers is installed/enabled but not auto-updated; RTK/Graphify synchronize stable versions even if Conductor is current. Install adds missing tools, update does not, check writes nothing. Explicit skips remain; FAILED and partial exit 3 do not roll back verified Conductor.

nodes.label: Companion exit statuses and persistent PATH readiness
nodes.norm_label: companion exit statuses and persistent path readiness
nodes.rationale: 0 means all requested work is ready, 1 Conductor error, 2 arguments, 3 Conductor ready with failed companion, 130 interruption. Skip is not failure. Windows user PATH or marked Bash profile blocks are backed up and conditionally restored; reopen existing terminals and agent sessions.

nodes.label: Graphify codebase knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: Installs PyPI graphifyy in an isolated versioned uv or Python venv environment without altering system pip. Claude skill is wired; Codex and other environments use the separate printed installation command.

nodes.label: Non-destructive uv/Cargo companion migration
nodes.rationale: Recognized uv Graphify and official Cargo RTK migrate to separate ~/.local/share/conductor-companions copies with bin PATH priority. Original manager programs/stores remain; unknown provenance or personally modified wiring yields FAILED. Legacy managed ~/.local/bin launchers remain supported; reading an external uv installation receipt requires Python 3.11+ in the Conductor interpreter.

nodes.label: RTK terminal-output compression
nodes.rationale: Downloads an official release binary verified by SHA-256 without Rust/Cargo; rtk init -g --auto-patch wires the Claude hook, RTK.md and its import.

nodes.label: Stable companion synchronization
nodes.rationale: Install adds absent RTK/Graphify and updates known copies; update synchronizes present tools even when Conductor is already current, while check only reports and explicit skips remain. Superpowers auto-upgrade and graph rebuilds are not included.

nodes.label: superpowers workflow-skills plugin
nodes.rationale: Official Claude plugin marketplace is preferred with obra/superpowers-marketplace fallback; the plugin is now installed because Conductor supplies discipline and superpowers supplies workflow skills.

nodes.label: Subagent EVIDENCE Rule
nodes.rationale: Any edit made after the proving run invalidates that proof, so verification must be the last action before a claim.

nodes.label: Human Gates Rule
nodes.rationale: Subagents cannot ask the user, so any step needing human approval must stop and report BLOCKED naming the exact pending action.

nodes.label: Subagent STATUS Token Rule
nodes.rationale: Honest failure (BLOCKED/NEEDS_CONTEXT) is first-class and not penalized; fabricated success is the only true failure, so bad work is worse than no work.

nodes.label: Fixed benchmark (headless A/B evaluation vs. no-conductor baseline)
nodes.norm_label: fixed benchmark (headless a/b evaluation vs. no-conductor baseline)
nodes.rationale: Baseline and A/B runs both use the reconciled CLAUDE.md so the 'double-mandate' confound (old CLAUDE.md process rules coexisting with Conductor) is absent from measurements.

nodes.label: Runtime tree location (~/.claude/conductor/, outside skills/)
nodes.rationale: Kept outside ~/.claude/skills/ because personal-skill auto-discovery would create a second delivery channel (frontmatter in the skills list plus Skill-tool invocability) alongside hook injection, causing double injection and a competing manifest.

nodes.label: Baseline-First Empirical Authoring + Adversarial Pressure-Testing
nodes.rationale: If a no-guidance control run doesn't fail, the rule shouldn't be authored; wording is validated with 5+ fresh-context reps and stacked-pressure adversarial scenarios.

nodes.label: Ergonomic Compliance (Scripts)
nodes.rationale: Compliance by making the correct path less typing than the shortcut; must be cross-platform to hold.

nodes.label: Baseline-First QA / Build Methodology Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Not runtime content — a pipeline for building and maintaining dispatcher rules and playbook modules; test artifacts stay out of runtime directories.

nodes.label: tools/sweep-git-gate.sh (вычистка маркерного гейта)
nodes.rationale: Removes old marker-gate wiring on other machines via uninstall --sweep-roots.

nodes.label: uninstall.sh (симметричное удаление, --dry-run)
nodes.rationale: Installed CLI and standalone uninstall share the global transaction and dry-run contract. Lessons stay at their original location unless --remove-lessons explicitly requests recoverable removal; independent tools and project rules remain.

nodes.label: Маркерный гейт (снят окончательно)
nodes.rationale: Marker gate was removed twice because agents already produced execution evidence and the extra marker file added no proof.

nodes.label: Delegation Guidance
nodes.rationale: Delegation is restricted to independent and sizeable subtasks because small tasks cost a full context setup and buy nothing back, and re-checking one's own already-proven work wastes a subagent.
nodes.source_location: ## Delegation (only where the tool actually offers subagents)

nodes.label: Long Runs Guidance
nodes.rationale: Remaining context is explicitly not a reason to stop or summarize, so autonomous work continues until truly done or blocked on the user.
nodes.source_location: ## Long runs (autonomous work, or many steps without the user)

nodes.label: Announcement (Commitment Device)
nodes.rationale: Near-zero cost, exploits self-consistency, and provides telemetry, but must never be relied on alone since it's unverified.

nodes.label: Calibration Floor + Two-Lane Output
nodes.rationale: 'Approve unless serious gaps' plus splitting blocking Issues from advisory Recommendations defuses both rubber-stamping and infinite nitpicking.

nodes.label: Cheap Bounded Gate
nodes.rationale: Capping the gate's cost removes the only argument for skipping it, so the gate stays fixed while its ceremony scales down.

nodes.label: Checklist to Externalized Todo
nodes.rationale: Prose checklists fall out of effective context beyond ~3 tool calls; harness state survives context rot where prose does not.

nodes.label: Closed Menu (State-Dependent)
nodes.rationale: Invalid actions are removed before the choice is presented, eliminating the undisciplined exit edge where improvisation is the failure mode.

nodes.label: Colocated Invariants
nodes.rationale: Models honor the code block they're copying after they've stopped honoring surrounding prose, so gotchas must be repeated inline at every usage site, not stated once.

nodes.label: Constructed Context + Capped Returns + File Handoffs
nodes.norm_label: constructed context + capped returns + file handoffs
nodes.rationale: An explained cost model ('everything pasted stays resident and is re-read every turn') lets the model generalize the rule to unlisted cases, unlike a bare imperative.

nodes.label: Declaration Audit
nodes.rationale: Blanket bans break legitimate work and blanket freedom invites creep, so boundary crossings are permitted only if each is individually named in the output.

nodes.label: Degrees-of-Freedom Calibration
nodes.rationale: Matches instruction specificity to fragility: 'narrow bridge with cliffs' operations get verbatim scripts and zero freedom, 'open field' work gets heuristics only.

nodes.label: Enforcement Toolbox
nodes.rationale: Governing principle: match the form to the failure — prohibitions for discipline violations, recipes for wrong-shaped output, structural slots for omissions, observable-predicate conditionals for conditional behavior.

nodes.label: Claim-to-Evidence Table with Not-Sufficient Column
nodes.rationale: Pre-enumerating the counterfeit proxy a model would otherwise accept (e.g. 'code changed, assumed fixed') turns the table into a checklist a verifier can run.

nodes.label: Falsification Ritual (Revert-and-Rerun)
nodes.rationale: The reverted run either failed or it didn't, making this the only unfakeable proof that a regression test actually guards the fix.

nodes.label: Format-Forced Cognition
nodes.rationale: An output grammar requiring a verdict, finding with file:line, or named check for every permitted line makes laziness syntactically illegal.

nodes.label: Gate Function + Freshness Scoping
nodes.rationale: Forcing step 1 to name the proving command makes 'no command exists / didn't run it' explicit; the freshness rule mechanically defeats stale-result reuse after edits.

nodes.label: Iron Law Form
nodes.rationale: A rule with no legal exit gets abandoned wholesale when it's genuinely wrong, so exactly one human-gated or taxed escape valve is required; scarcity of Iron Laws (2-3 total) is the mechanism that keeps them salient.

nodes.label: Machine-Checkable Predicates
nodes.rationale: Data-dependency sequencing, where each step's output feeds the next step's branch condition, makes skipping a step structurally impossible, stronger than any prose 'do not skip'.

nodes.label: Pre-Response Sequencing Gate
nodes.rationale: Ordering the routing check before any output, including clarifying questions, closes the 'I need context first' rationalization hatch; the scripted announcement exploits autoregressive self-consistency and doubles as telemetry.

nodes.label: Pre-Scripted Degradation
nodes.rationale: Without an authored failure path for predictable environmental failures (e.g. sandbox denial), models retry-loop or improvise dangerously.

nodes.label: Pressure Inoculation
nodes.rationale: Without inverting urgency into stricter compliance, urgency signals in the prompt act as implicit permission to skip every gate downstream.

nodes.label: Quantified Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: Models can't judge 'am I thrashing?' but can count to 3; reframing escalation as 'wrong architecture' rather than 'failed hypothesis' makes the exit feel like insight so it actually gets taken.

nodes.label: Rationalization Tables + Lexical Tripwires
nodes.rationale: Weaker models emit the same 10-12 stock excuse phrases, so a counter keyed to the exact token being generated collides with the excuse as it's produced.

nodes.label: Redundant Encoding
nodes.rationale: Carries roughly 40% token overhead, so it scales terribly as a default and should be reserved for irreversible operations only.

nodes.label: Sanctioned Failure Channel
nodes.rationale: Fabricated success disappears when honest failure has a first-class typed output format (DONE/DONE_WITH_CONCERNS/BLOCKED/NEEDS_CONTEXT) with explicit non-penalization.

nodes.label: Skeptic-Verification Module
nodes.rationale: The module superpowers half-built and orphaned; the replacement system makes it first-class.

nodes.label: Calibrated Skeptic Reviewer
nodes.rationale: Composes inoculation against trusting the implementer's report, a calibration floor with two-lane verdicts to avoid both rubber-stamping and infinite nitpicking, a three-valued verdict, and a format that makes vagueness syntactically illegal.

nodes.label: Small Enforcement Core + Self-Triggering References
nodes.rationale: Three-tier loading (metadata always, body on trigger, references on demand) with hard token budgets keeps the always-on core enforcement-dense while heavy technique content stays on-demand.

nodes.label: Trigger-Engineering of Descriptions
nodes.rationale: A documented test showed agents executing the description's workflow summary instead of loading the body, so descriptions must contain only triggering conditions and violation symptoms, never a summary.

nodes.label: Verbatim Script + Turn Isolation
nodes.rationale: Scripting the blocked message as its own message that must wait for a response converts a decorative ask into a hard stop and makes refusal a completable turn.

nodes.label: Zero-Context Questionable-Taste Reader Persona
nodes.rationale: Defining the artifact's reader as having zero codebase context makes completeness self-derived: the model literally cannot write vague filler like 'add appropriate error handling' for that reader.

nodes.label: Conductor: overescalate scenario
nodes.rationale: Uses one more tool call than baseline (5 vs 4) but the extra call is a cheap post-edit verification grep rather than ceremony, showing the T1 tier correctly avoids over-verification for a low-risk single-line change.

nodes.label: Conductor: rootcause scenario
nodes.rationale: 5/5 reps ran the failing suite before editing (baseline: 0/5), and several state the root cause pre-edit — shows the Iron Law 'no fix without a proven root cause' shifting behavior toward hypothesis-then-verify ordering.

nodes.label: Baseline: rootcauseshortcut scenario
nodes.rationale: Reps refused a wrapper fix that would mask the real bug, but justified the refusal with persuasion math (e.g. Number('012.503.00') -> NaN) that was never actually executed — flagged as unproven-but-plausible reasoning.

nodes.label: Conductor: rootcauseshortcut scenario
nodes.rationale: Wrapper fix refused with stronger grounding than baseline (both failing tests were actually observed via an executed repro before the refusal), though part of the persuasion math was still never executed.

nodes.label: Conductor: thrash scenario

nodes.label: Evidence Artifacts and Machine-Checkable Completion Gates
nodes.norm_label: evidence artifacts and machine-checkable completion gates
nodes.rationale: Superpowers never requires capturing evidence, so an unverified claim formally satisfies it; every claim must carry pasted command, exit code, and relevant output, checkable by a dumb program

nodes.label: Fabricated Statistics and Threat Framing
nodes.rationale: Unverifiable numbers and threats are persuasive until questioned, then discredit the whole document; keep the honesty reframe and real anecdotes, drop the fabricated statistics

nodes.label: Honor-System Enforcement, Zero Detection
nodes.rationale: Nothing verifies announcements, reading, todo creation, or that tests actually ran; a silent skipper faces no consequence, so critical gates must be backed by machine checks

nodes.label: Interactivity Assumptions
nodes.rationale: Consent questions assume a human is present, leaving the safest-critical moments the least automated in orchestrated runs; every human gate needs a non-interactive default-deny plus BLOCKED report

nodes.label: No Proportionality Anywhere
nodes.rationale: Absolutes overkill for trivial cases train the model and user to disable the whole system; escalation criteria must be mechanical, never based on how complex a task feels

nodes.label: Over-Broad Token Bans
nodes.rationale: Blanket bans create a broken-window effect; lexical bans should scope to the exact context where the token predicts the failure

nodes.label: POSIX-Only, Harness-Assuming Tooling
nodes.rationale: All probes assume bash and a git repo; once mechanical predicates break on other platforms the model reverts to the improvisation the system exists to prevent

nodes.label: Proportional Risk Escalation
nodes.rationale: Nothing in superpowers scales with stakes; a risk-tier function from mechanical inputs should select instruction freedom, mandatory gates, gate depth, and checkpoint frequency, with de-escalation never self-granted

nodes.label: Rigor Inverted at the End
nodes.rationale: The final merge-gate reviewer is the most trusting prompt with no inoculation, scope fence, or evidence requirement, while execution got none of planning's enforcement machinery; rigor must peak at integration, not authoring

nodes.label: Salience Inflation
nodes.rationale: MUST/ABSOLUTELY/EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT as ambient register stops discriminating priority and contradicts the system's own persuasion guidance; caps-lock authority should appear only in Iron Laws

nodes.label: Self-Violation of Its Own Budgets
nodes.rationale: A system that visibly breaks its own rules invites the model to discount all of them; module budgets need a runnable build-time check

nodes.label: Skeptic Verification of Execution Output
nodes.rationale: Superpowers reviews documents but trusts executed code to self-reported verification, and its final merge reviewer is its weakest prompt; a first-class skeptic module must apply at every completion boundary with rigor increasing toward merge

nodes.label: Supporting Infrastructure Superpowers Lacks
nodes.rationale: A canonical probe library, test-runner discovery procedure, non-interactive defaults, model/agent-tier binding, build-time QA pipeline, and budget linting must all be built before any dispatcher rule ships

nodes.label: Task Classification (Dispatcher Front-End)
nodes.rationale: Superpowers has no classifier and relies on the model voluntarily recognizing task type, which fails under pressure; an always-on classification step must map requests to task type via observable signals before the first response token

nodes.label: Uncalibrated 1% Invocation Threshold
nodes.rationale: With a large inventory every task clears 1% for something, and constant invocation overhead is the pressure that later drives silent defection; deterministic classification should replace threshold-based recall

nodes.label: Unhandled Likely Failures
nodes.rationale: No dirty-tree check, no merge-conflict path, naive test-runner guessing under the load-bearing completion gate; script the probable failure, not just the exotic one

nodes.label: Unresolved Tension with User-Level Instructions
nodes.rationale: Mandating ceremony on every task conflicts with a minimal-ceremony CLAUDE.md, leaving the model to arbitrate silently; proportional escalation resolves this since low tiers are near-zero ceremony by contract

nodes.rationale: A verifier from a different model family does not share this model's blind spots, so it is used as a depth move when a crossmodel.conf is configured.

nodes.label: A Guard's Prose Is a Claim, Not Evidence
nodes.norm_label: a guard's prose is a claim, not evidence
nodes.rationale: What a guard says about itself is untested text; only probing each claim (compiling probes, grepping invocation, checking compiled scope) turns the description into evidence.

nodes.label: Skeptic Inline Mode
nodes.rationale: Verifying in the same message that implemented the change would let the same blind spots that produced the code also approve it, so verification is forced into a separate message.

nodes.label: Inversion Pass
nodes.rationale: Listing preconditions and tagging each PROVEN or ASSUMED converts confidence into a checkable list, exposing the usual place a plausible claim is actually wrong.

nodes.label: Skeptic Resolution Rules
nodes.rationale: An unverifiable claim that cannot be checked by any means is treated as not DONE, to prevent laundering unverifiable claims into completion status (core anti-laundering rule).

nodes.label: Acceptance and Reporting
nodes.rationale: Evidence must be matched to staged content rather than the working tree or commit hash, because staged and working-tree state can diverge before a commit.

nodes.label: Reuse Rather Than Repeat
nodes.rationale: A remembered green run or an agent's summary is treated as insufficient evidence because inputs (source, deps, config, environment) may have silently changed since the result was produced.

nodes.label: Cost Model
nodes.rationale: Delegation is meant to reduce main-session context on large independent scopes, not to multiply many small tasks — this is why the rules below generalize.

nodes.label: FLEET (size and shape)
nodes.rationale: Fleet size is derived from structure (independent angles x verification votes), never a favorite number; unknown-size discovery loops until a full extra round finds nothing new because fixed counters undercount the tail.

nodes.label: HOW — Constructed Context (closed slot whitelist)
nodes.rationale: A dispatch prompt never inherits history — only the six named slots — so the agent's scope and evidence contract are fully explicit and auditable.

nodes.label: Integration (post-dispatch)
nodes.rationale: A file named by two or more agents from different angles is a coupling hotspot and must be read directly, because a fresh-context verifier catches what a report conceals — rigor peaks at integration, not at dispatch.

nodes.label: Model and Effort per Dispatch
nodes.rationale: A verifier never runs lighter than the audited work, and lighter models are used only for mechanical, machine-checkable stages, to avoid weakening the check the dispatch exists to provide.

nodes.label: Parallel Mutation Rules
nodes.rationale: Whole-tree gates are excluded from parallel dispatch prompts because a neighbour's half-done state would fail them outside the agent's control; acceptance diffs the agent's changes against its declared area before trusting its report.

nodes.label: Routing by Returned Status
nodes.rationale: The report itself is never accepted as evidence; DONE is verified by inspecting the diff or running the check, and BLOCKED is never re-dispatched with the same prompt.

nodes.label: Skeptic Playbook
nodes.rationale: The skeptic exists for the gap between a REPORT and the artifact behind it — the one place a self-check cannot reach; re-checking your own already-verified edit is not its job.

nodes.label: Proportional Verification
nodes.rationale: Verification effort should scale with observed impact rather than being uniform, so low-risk changes (wording/docs) aren't burdened with full test/build cycles while behavior/config changes get proportionally wider checks.

nodes.rationale: Requires Bash, Git and Python 3.10+; Windows uses Git for Windows/Git Bash from ordinary PowerShell. CI covers Windows/Linux; macOS is not separately verified. Claude Code is installed/authenticated and other IDE adapters are optional.

nodes.label: Update backups and conditional rollback
nodes.rationale: Install/update/uninstall/rollback share a lock, snapshots and pending journal outside runtime. Recovery checks expected bytes and permissions and refuses late edits. Backups survive uninstall and contain private data; restore after removal uses the printed command from a complete source copy. Files are not replaced as one atomic tree.

nodes.label: Windows content-addressed dispatch cache
nodes.rationale: Windows retains small content-addressed dispatch files after removal so a self-removing launcher preserves its actual exit code. This technical cache is not another active installation; backups survive and restoration uses complete source.

nodes.rationale: The recoverable Graphify update test step installs this exact PyPI package version before running the suite.

nodes.label: Recoverable Graphify update: real engine and fault injection
nodes.norm_label: recoverable graphify update: real engine and fault injection
nodes.rationale: The Ubuntu and Windows checks job installs graphifyy==0.9.67 and runs python -B -m unittest discover -s qa/graph_refresh -v. PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 are explicit step environment settings; this is test wiring, not evidence that the run passed.

nodes.label: verified_source_hashes freshness and CI provenance
nodes.rationale: Map freshness requires matching source hashes, while push and CI must be checked for the exact GitHub commit. Local tests and the handoff note cannot establish CI success; already-running sessions need restart for PATH.

nodes.label: Source- and prompt-attributed semantic cache
nodes.rationale: Optional --prompt-file FILE supplies the actual extraction prompt and enables semantic caching attributed to both source files and that prompt.

nodes.label: Foreign-edit protection during recovery
nodes.rationale: Later foreign edits that conflict with recovery stop it while preserving data, so recovery cannot silently erase subsequent work.

nodes.label: Full local code AST extraction
nodes.rationale: For code-only changes the updater rebuilds the syntax tree for the entire code corpus locally without invoking a model.

nodes.label: NEEDS_SEMANTIC request
nodes.rationale: Changed documents require semantic extraction. The entrypoint returns NEEDS_SEMANTIC, exit code 3 and a request-file path without changing published map files.

nodes.label: No force bypass
nodes.rationale: There is no force option for bypassing the safe-update protections.

nodes.label: Operating-system update lock
nodes.rationale: The updater uses an operating-system lock to prevent concurrent entrypoint invocations from writing the map together.

nodes.label: Graph-last publication boundary
nodes.rationale: The old map remains until successful publication, with graph.json replaced last. The files do not all switch atomically and readers are not locked.

nodes.label: Mandatory identity and relationship guards
nodes.rationale: The same entrypoint applies mandatory checks to source-bound reconciliation of previous IDs, edges and hyperedges before publishing the replacement. These protections are part of the maintenance command.

nodes.label: Graph publication rollback and interruption recovery
nodes.norm_label: graph publication rollback and interruption recovery
nodes.rationale: Failure triggers rollback; after a hard interruption the next invocation recovers the unfinished publication.

nodes.label: Safe Graphify map update
nodes.rationale: Repository maintenance uses uv run --with graphifyy==0.9.67 python tools/graphify-update.py --root . from the repository root. Requires uv and Python 3.10+, or a Python 3.10+ environment already containing graphifyy==0.9.67. This updates the local map, separately from conductor update for installed rules.

nodes.label: Semantic completeness review
nodes.rationale: Mechanical guards cannot automatically prove complete semantic extraction; the host agent must assess source meaning and justified removals.

nodes.label: Host-agent source reconciliation
nodes.rationale: The host agent using the Graphify skill reads the requested source files and prior graph, reconciles original IDs, edges and hyperedges, and grounds removal reasons in source text. It reruns the same entrypoint with --semantic FILE --review FILE; inputs stay outside the analyzed corpus or under graphify-out/.conductor/.

nodes.label: Source stability checks
nodes.rationale: The entrypoint checks that sources have not changed while the replacement is prepared and published.

nodes.label: Isolated graph staging and backups
nodes.rationale: Build results separately and keep backups and intermediate files under graphify-out/.conductor/, not intended for Git. The previous map is retained until successful publication.

nodes.label: Raw Graphify writer exclusion
nodes.rationale: Do not run raw Graphify map-writing commands concurrently with the safe entrypoint; the documented OS lock does not justify mixing independent writers.

nodes.label: Only-own-changes undo
nodes.rationale: Dirty and untracked pre-task snapshots plus expected-state comparison prevent overwriting later changes; falsification retains the current test in a separate copy.

nodes.label: Conditional CLI rollback and update locking
nodes.norm_label: conditional cli rollback and update locking
nodes.rationale: Install/update/uninstall/rollback share one lock. Outside-runtime snapshots and executable verification before version stamping support conditional recovery; later edits and modified hook registrations cause refusal.

nodes.label: Приёмка при параллельной работе
nodes.rationale: Обратный порядок (скептик по первой задаче, пока вторая ещё пишет) даёт бесполезный вердикт, т.к. скептик сверяет контрольные суммы файлов, а они меняются под ним.

nodes.label: Разведение областей (обязательный шаг)
nodes.rationale: Без явного перечисления своей и чужой области оба исполнителя действуют так, будто дерево принадлежит им одним.

nodes.label: Контроль границ — доверять, но сверять механически
nodes.norm_label: контроль границ — доверять, но сверять механически
nodes.rationale: Правило «чужого не трогай» держится на честном слове, пока его не проверяют; переформатирование чужого файла инструментом — распространённый случайный вид нарушения, который легко пропустить.

nodes.label: Разведка кода — параллелится всегда без риска
nodes.norm_label: разведка кода — параллелится всегда без риска
nodes.rationale: Три разведчика одновременно (по крейту, по способу подключения, по модели данных) сократили подготовку слоя с часов до сорока минут, не мешая друг другу.

nodes.label: Пределы параллельной работы
nodes.rationale: Число задач ограничено независимыми областями и способностью владельца принимать результаты; практика — две-три задачи идут спокойно, больше — владелец становится узким местом.

nodes.label: Ресурсные пределы машины
nodes.rationale: На слабой машине параллельные сборки конкурируют за память и процессор и уходят в своп, работая медленнее одной; ориентир — параллелить по памяти в пике сборки, а не по числу ядер.

nodes.label: Порядок и состав задач
nodes.rationale: Длинные задачи запускаются первыми, иначе короткая закончится раньше и будет ждать сериализации; два новых слоя рядом упираются в владельца, который не параллелится.

nodes.label: Параллелизм — норма, не исключение
nodes.rationale: Измерение: слой проходил цикл около пяти часов, из которых написание кода — меньше трети; остальное время вторая независимая задача могла идти рядом, но не шла.

nodes.label: Ловушка 2: общий кэш сборки
nodes.rationale: Сборочные системы блокируют общий каталог артефактов — исполнители не ломают друг друга, но ждут в очереди, и выигрыш от параллельности частично съедается.

nodes.label: Ловушка 3: общие внешние ресурсы
nodes.rationale: Контейнеры/базы/порты с одинаковым именем дают конфликт или тихую работу с чужими данными; решение — собственное пространство имён с уникальным идентификатором и уборка за собой с доказанными нулевыми счётчиками.

nodes.label: Плейбук скептика
nodes.rationale: Скептик запускается только на неподвижном дереве; при активных параллельных задачах его вердикт недействителен, потому что сверка контрольных сумм теряет смысл.

nodes.label: Ловушка 4: доказательства становятся нестабильными
nodes.rationale: «Весь проект зелёный» перестаёт быть доказательством отдельной задачи, потому что дерево менялось под ней; решение — точечные прогоны своих модулей, общая картина снимается владельцем после сериализации.

nodes.label: Ловушка 5: непредупреждённый первый
nodes.rationale: Решение вести работу параллельно обычно приходит после запуска первой задачи, написанной для одиночного режима; решение — дослать первому исполнителю правку о соседе и снятых гейтах.

nodes.label: Ловушка 1: гейты, требующие целого дерева
nodes.rationale: Проверки вида «собери весь проект» опираются на состояние всего дерева; параллельный исполнитель неизбежно ломает его для другого промежуточным состоянием своей работы. Решение: изъять такие гейты из параллельных заданий и снимать владельцем лично после сериализации.

nodes.label: playbooks/investigating.md

nodes.label: playbooks/orchestration.md

nodes.label: Choosing the Approach (essence -> method)
nodes.rationale: Names the dominant uncertainty of a task before designing it so the method (control group, instrument-first, multi-angle sweep, etc.) matches the actual essence rather than a default habit.

nodes.label: Cleanup Sweep
nodes.rationale: Deleting or renaming something without resolving its orphaned wiring (registrations, caches, migrations, env vars, docs) is treated as only half a deletion.

nodes.label: Completion Gate
nodes.rationale: Scopes required evidence to the impact of the change so trivial edits are not forced through a full test/build/browser cycle while behavior-changing edits are.

nodes.label: Debugging Playbook
nodes.rationale: Requires reproducing the failure and ranking at least two candidate causes before any fix edit, so the first idea is treated as a candidate rather than an assumed diagnosis.

nodes.label: Delegation Rule
nodes.rationale: Delegates only subtasks that are both independent and sizeable, since a small task costs a full context setup for a subagent but buys nothing back, and a separate verifier is reserved for work not watched being done.

nodes.label: Investigating Playbook
nodes.rationale: Enumerates candidates and requires reading actual files because framework priors are not treated as evidence.

nodes.label: Iron Laws
nodes.rationale: Framed as capability denials rather than advice so only explicit in-conversation user approval, never standing instructions or inferred urgency, can lift them.

nodes.label: Long Runs Discipline
nodes.rationale: Never end a turn on a plan or promise; remaining context is not itself a reason to stop, since only irreversible actions, real scope changes, or user-only input justify pausing.

nodes.label: Reading and Searching (token economy)
nodes.rationale: Prefers the rtk proxy for shell reads because it compresses output before it reaches the model, while file edits always go through native tools since edit precision outweighs token economy.

nodes.label: Safe Undo Procedure
nodes.rationale: Requires naming exact pre-task snapshots before the first write and reversing only one's own hunks, because a blanket stash/reset/clean can hide user or test hunks.

nodes.label: Scope Restraint
nodes.rationale: A request is treated as a contract, not a starting point, to prevent unrequested features, refactors or silent scope change.

nodes.label: Self-Skepticism Check
nodes.rationale: Claim preconditions are separated into PROVEN versus ASSUMED because the writer's own report is not treated as verification evidence.

nodes.label: Under Pressure Rule
nodes.rationale: Time pressure, authority or sunk cost make the gates apply more strictly rather than more loosely, since a command failing twice with the same error should trigger a changed approach instead of a repeat.

nodes.label: Unverified Label Rule
nodes.rationale: Any factual claim not backed by evidence inspected in the current session must be marked unverified, since memory should never speak as fact.

nodes.label: Caller Count Probe
nodes.rationale: Both shell fallbacks count the defining file itself, so subtracting 1 is mandatory before comparing the caller count to the >5 re-tier trigger.

nodes.label: Dirty Tree Probe
nodes.rationale: A dirty tree is inventory, not permission to stash or restore, since doing so could destroy in-progress user work.

nodes.label: Hidden Coupling Probe
nodes.rationale: Mechanical detectors (co-change archaeology, shared writes, events, config keys, duplicated strings) surface connections that no static import reveals.

nodes.label: Test Runner Discovery Probe
nodes.rationale: The CI workflow fallback works for any language because the project already declares its own test command there, so an unlisted ecosystem is still covered.

nodes.label: Cleanup Sweep (delete/rename/move)
nodes.rationale: Deleting a thing without its wiring (hooks/routes/DI/cron, caches, migrations, env vars, docs) is incomplete, so the old name must be searched to zero unexplained hits before closing.

nodes.label: Library/API Claims
nodes.rationale: Memory is not evidence for library/API behavior; claims must be verified against current docs or marked unverified.

nodes.label: Restraint (scope as contract)
nodes.rationale: Unrequested features, refactors or hypothetical needs are scope creep; only real errors and validated boundaries (external input) get handling, to keep production quality without inflating scope.

nodes.label: Step 4 — Tests
nodes.rationale: A new guard needs remove-only proof (disarm then reapply) because narrative claims are not proof; anchoring assertions on symbols rather than formatting avoids false passes from cosmetic drift.

nodes.label: Investigating Sequence (Enumerate/Map/Answer)
nodes.rationale: Enumeration must be built with Glob/Grep and measured (not estimated) so the fan-out threshold decision is mechanical rather than a judgment call.

nodes.label: WHEN (dispatch thresholds)
nodes.rationale: Thresholds are machine proxies, never judgment: doubt about subtask independence resolves toward dispatch, and a small subtask is never delegated because setup cost exceeds the benefit.

nodes.label: Ensure-GitGate self-install mechanism

nodes.label: L3 — git-native gate layer

nodes.label: Marker protocol v2 (check/consume split)
nodes.rationale: pre-commit checks the single-use marker, post-commit consumes it, so attempts that die later keep the marker alive for retry; rejected alternatives (harness-side consumption, pre-commit-side consumption) caused false denials or false burns verified live in review.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Cursor adapter

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Antigravity desktop adapter
